summary: Before Manchester United's Sunday derby against Manchester City, Erik ten Hag rejected Jamie Carragher's claim that United are going backwards, citing pressing and ball-regain statistics. Sky Sports' Sam Blitz checked the numbers: United lead in final-third possessions won and high turnovers, but rank only 10th in PPDA and have scored no goals from 104 high turnovers. Ten Hag also addressed the forwards' poor scoring and said he still backs Marcus Rashford.
one_line: Ten Hag disputes Carragher's claim that Man Utd have regressed, citing pressing stats, while admitting problems with possession and forwards' finishing before the City derby.
key_facts: Erik ten Hag disagreed with Jamie Carragher's Daily Telegraph column claim that Manchester United are going backwards this season.
Carragher wrote that United's summer signings have made the club 'stale' and that Ten Hag should be questioned on whether he can get the best out of his squad.
Ten Hag said United are top of the Premier League in high ball regains and top in middle-of-the-pitch ball regains, and that the pressing is very good.
Sky Sports' Sam Blitz found Ten Hag slightly wrong on middle-third regains: United are second behind Everton.
United are top of the Premier League for possessions won in the final third and high turnovers.
United's PPDA ranks 10th in the league, which is average, meaning opponents often keep the ball and play around United's pressing forwards.
United have the fourth-highest number of shots after winning the ball in their final third, but have scored no goals from 104 high turnovers.
United won three straight games against Brentford, Sheffield United and FC Copenhagen, though the performances were far from convincing.
Christian Eriksen said United still need to find their 'balance and routines'; Ten Hag cited Arsenal away and the first 30 minutes at Bayern Munich as examples of inconsistent possession play.
Manchester City have the highest number of build-up attacks in the Premier League this season.
Erling Haaland has scored 9 Premier League goals this season, more than United's five forwards combined in all competitions (8).
Casemiro, a defensive midfielder, is United's top scorer this season with four goals.
Marcus Rashford has one goal this season after scoring 30 last season, but Ten Hag has strong belief he will return to scoring a lot of goals.
